metadata.title: feat(security): implement nonce-based CSP to remove unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval from current policy
metadata.author: bogdanmariusc10

description:
## 🔗 Related Issue
Closes #4330
**Jira Issue:** https://jsw.ibm.com/browse/ICACF-26

---

## 📝 Summary

This PR implements a comprehensive Content Security Policy (CSP) solution that removes `unsafe-inline` and `unsafe-eval` directives, addressing security vulnerabilities identified in the pentesting report.

**What changed:**
- Removed `unsafe-inline` from `script-src` directive (prevents XSS attacks)
- Removed `unsafe-eval` entirely from CSP (blocks dynamic code execution)
- Implemented cryptographically secure nonce-based CSP using `secrets.token_urlsafe(16)` (128 bits of entropy per request)
- Added `'unsafe-hashes'` to `script-src` for inline event handlers (onclick, onload, etc.)
- Configured HTMX 2.0.3 to use CSP nonces via `htmx.config.inlineScriptNonce`
- Kept `'unsafe-inline'` for `style-src` only (required for Alpine.js dynamic inline styles)

**Why this matters:**
- **Prevents XSS attacks** - Only scripts with matching nonces can execute, blocking malicious inline script injection
- **Blocks dynamic code execution** - eval(), Function constructor, and similar dangerous functions are now blocked
- **Follows OWASP best practices** - Modern nonce-based CSP is the recommended approach for securing web applications
- **HTMX 2.0.3 compatibility** - No longer uses eval(), making it CSP-compliant

---

## 🏷️ Type of Change
- [x] Feature / Enhancement
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Chore (deps, CI, tooling)
- [ ] Other (describe below)

---

## 🧪 Verification

| Check                     | Command         | Status |
|---------------------------|-----------------|--------|
| Formatting                | `make black isort autoflake` | ✅ PASS |
| Linting                   | `make ruff`     | ✅ PASS |
| Admin UI                  | Manual testing  | ✅ PASS |

---

## ✅ Checklist
- [x] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`)
- [x] Tests added/updated for changes
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] No secrets or credentials committed

---

## 📓 Notes

### Security Impact

**Before:**
```
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' ...
```
- ❌ Any inline script could execute (XSS vulnerability)
- ❌ eval() and similar functions allowed (code injection risk)

**After:**
```
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' 'nonce-ABC123...' 'unsafe-hashes' https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com ...
                         style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com ...
```
- ✅ Only scripts with matching nonce can execute
- ✅ eval() and similar functions blocked
- ✅ Unique nonce per request (128 bits of entropy)
- ✅ Inline event handlers allowed via `'unsafe-hashes'`
- ✅ Alpine.js dynamic styles work via `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`

### Implementation Details

**Core CSP Implementation** ([`mcpgateway/middleware/security_headers.py:295-311`](mcpgateway/middleware/security_headers.py:295-311)):
- Generates cryptographically secure nonce per request using `secrets.token_urlsafe(16)`
- Stores nonce in `request.state.csp_nonce` for template access
- Configures CSP directives with nonce-based script-src
- Separates style-src to allow `'unsafe-inline'` (Alpine.js requirement)

**HTMX Configuration** ([`mcpgateway/templates/admin.html:321-327`](mcpgateway/templates/admin.html:321-327)):
- Sets `window.htmxConfig.inlineScriptNonce` before HTMX bundle loads
- Allows HTMX inline event handlers (hx-on:*) to work with strict CSP

**HTMX Nonce Application** ([`mcpgateway/admin_ui/admin.js:15-19`](mcpgateway/admin_ui/admin.js:15-19)):
- Reads nonce from `window.htmxConfig` and applies to `htmx.config.inlineScriptNonce`
- Ensures all HTMX-generated inline scripts include the nonce

**Files Modified:**
- `mcpgateway/middleware/security_headers.py` - Core CSP with nonce generation
- `mcpgateway/templates/admin.html` - HTMX nonce configuration
- `mcpgateway/admin_ui/admin.js` - Applied nonce to htmx.config
- `.secrets.baseline` - Updated baseline

### Technical Notes

**HTMX 2.0.3 Compatibility:**
- HTMX 2.0 removed eval() usage, making it CSP-compliant
- Inline event handlers (hx-on:*) require either nonces or `'unsafe-hashes'`
- We use both: nonces for explicit scripts, `'unsafe-hashes'` for inline handlers

**Alpine.js Requirement:**
- Alpine.js generates dynamic inline styles at runtime
- Requires `'unsafe-inline'` in `style-src` (cannot use nonces for styles)
- This is an acceptable security trade-off for UI framework functionality

**Security Trade-offs:**
- `'unsafe-hashes'` allows inline event handlers (onclick, etc.) - acceptable for trusted admin UI
- `'unsafe-inline'` for styles only - lower risk than scripts
- No `'unsafe-eval'` - highest priority security improvement

### PenTest Findings Addressed

✅ **unsafe-inline removed from script-src** - Replaced with nonce-based whitelisting  
✅ **unsafe-eval removed entirely** - No dynamic code execution allowed  
✅ **Modern CSP implementation** - Follows OWASP best practices

reviews.author: marekdano
marekdano
reviews.body:
@bogdanmariusc10 - thanks for addressing the issues 

I found out:

#### Blocking Issues

  1. `'unsafe-hashes'` without accompanying hash values is a no-op

  The CSP keyword `'unsafe-hashes'` does not relax any policy on its own. It acts as a flag that enables hash-source tokens (`'sha256-...', 'sha384-...'`) to apply to inline event handlers rather than only to `<script>` elements. Without at least one accompanying hash in the directive, `'unsafe-hashes'` does nothing.
```bash
  script-src 'self' 'nonce-{csp_nonce}' 'unsafe-hashes'
```

  Either:
  - Compute and include the `SHA-256` hashes of each whitelisted inline event handler, or
  - Remove `'unsafe-hashes'` entirely — if all inline handlers have already been removed (as the diff claims), it is not needed.

  Leaving it in creates a misleading impression that event handlers are protected-by-hash when they are not.

  2. Stale `onclick` selector in `events.js` (line 499, current main branch)
```bash
  const gatewaysTab = document.querySelector('[onclick*="gateways"]');
  if (gatewaysTab) {
    gatewaysTab.addEventListener("click", function () {
      setTimeout(initializeCACertUpload, 100);
    });
  }
```

  The PR removes `onclick` attributes from sidebar links in `admin.html`, and it updates the tab-switch detection at line 597 to use `.sidebar-link`. But line 499 still queries by `onclick` attribute content. If the gateways sidebar link no longer has an `onclick` attribute, this silently returns `null`, and `initializeCACertUpload` is never re-triggered when the gateways tab is selected. This is a behavioral regression. It should be updated to the same class-based selector approach used for the tab-switch detection fix.

  3. Docstring examples in `security_headers.py` show the old unsafe CSP

  The doctest block (lines ~204–213 in the current file) includes:
```bash
  "script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com",
```

  If these doctests are run (they appear to be valid, executable doctests), they now document the pre-PR CSP, not the new nonce-based one. They should be updated to reflect the new directive or removed from the docstring.

  ---
  Significant Concerns

  4. `window.htmxConfig` bootstrapping is a load-order dependency

  `admin.js` reads `window.htmxConfig.inlineScriptNonce` to configure `HTMX`. For this to work, a template must emit:
```bash
  <script nonce="{{ csp_nonce(request) }}">
    window.htmxConfig = { inlineScriptNonce: "{{ csp_nonce(request) }}" };
  </script>
```

  before the bundled `admin.js` loads. This is an invisible load-order contract. If a template reorders script tags, HTMX silently loses the nonce and all HTMX-generated inline scripts will be blocked by the CSP. A comment in the template (or a console warning in `admin.js` when the config is missing) would make this dependency explicit.

  5. `'unsafe-inline'` retained in `style-src` is undocumented in the CSP string itself

  The PR is explicit in its commit messages that `unsafe-inline` is intentionally kept for Alpine.js dynamic styles. However, the CSP string in code has no comment explaining this exception. Given that the PR's headline is "remove unsafe-inline", a reviewer or future developer scanning the CSP header output will see 'unsafe-inline' and may not know it was a deliberate, reviewed compromise. A short inline comment would preserve intent.

  6. CDN sources in script-src without Subresource Integrity (SRI)

  The PR retains:
  `https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com https://cdn.tailwindcss.com https://cdn.jsdelivr.net https://unpkg.com`
  in `script-src`. These are explicit allowances for any script served from those CDNs. Nonces protect against injected inline scripts; they do not protect against CDN compromise. For external scripts loaded via `<script src="...">`, SRI
  (`integrity="sha384-..."`) is the appropriate countermeasure. This is not a regression introduced by this PR, but it is the natural next step given the security focus here.

  ---
  Minor Notes

  7. `csp_nonce` registered as a Jinja2 global taking request explicitly

  `jinja_env.globals["csp_nonce"] = get_csp_nonce_from_request`

  Templates call it as `{{ csp_nonce(request) }}`. This works but requires every template author to remember to pass request. A filter (`{{ request | csp_nonce }}`) or a context processor that injects the nonce string directly (so templates use` {{csp_nonce }}`, not a function call) would be harder to misuse. Not blocking, but worth considering if there are many templates to maintain.

---
#### Test Coverage Assessment

  - Integration test for header-template nonce consistency — critical. This test must verify that the nonce value in the Content-Security-Policy response header and the nonce attribute in <script nonce="..."> tags in the response body are
  identical. If it only checks that both exist (without comparing values), a mismatch could go undetected.

reviews.author: marekdano
reviews.body:
@bogdanmariusc10 - thanks for fixing the issue

There are minor issues that can be fixed in this PR, but are not blocking merging
I'm approving the PR.

 1. Class-level docstring uses nonce for style-src (`security_headers.py:66-71`)

  The class-level docstring example shows:
  `f"style-src 'self' 'nonce-{csp_nonce}'"`
  But the actual implementation (line 387) uses:
  `"style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://..."`
  This is a documentation inconsistency — the class-level doctest incorrectly implies `style-src` also uses nonces.
   The `dispatch()` method docstring at line 218 does this correctly. The class-level example should either match the real policy or be updated to match the dispatch docstring.

2.  Weak doctest assertion (`security_headers.py:231`)
```
  >>> "'unsafe-inline'" not in csp_header or "style-src" in csp_header
  True
```

  This assertion is always `True` because `"style-src"` is always in the header (short-circuit OR makes it vacuous).
  It does not actually verify that `'unsafe-inline'` is absent from `script-src`. The dispatch docstring could instead assert:
```
  >>> script_src = [d for d in csp_directives if "script-src" in d][0]
  >>> "'unsafe-inline'" not in script_src
  True 
```

LGTM 🚀

commits.message:
security: implement nonce-based CSP to remove unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval

- Remove 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' from Content-Security-Policy
- Implement cryptographically secure nonce generation per request (secrets.token_urlsafe(16))
- Add csp_nonce Jinja2 global function for template access
- Update 19 inline scripts across 13 templates with nonce attributes
- Fix CSP consistency test to validate structure instead of exact match
- Add type annotations to new helper functions

Addresses pen testing findings:
- Prevents XSS attacks via inline script injection
- Blocks dynamic code execution (eval, Function constructor)
- Follows OWASP CSP best practices

Files modified:
- mcpgateway/middleware/security_headers.py (CSP implementation)
- mcpgateway/main.py (Jinja2 global registration)
- mcpgateway/version.py (fallback template support)
- tests/security/test_security_headers.py (updated CSP test)
- 13 HTML templates (added nonce attributes)

All tests passing, code formatted and linted.

Signed-off-by: Bogdan-Marius-Catanus <bogdan-marius.catanus@ibm.com>
